findings.summary: The node's required artifact audits/methodology-compliance.md was never produced. The worktree's audits/ directory contains only design-review.md, and the subject diff (base b12fde4 -> tip eff0c06) lists exactly one added file: audits/design-review.md. The final compliance audit — the node's entire reason to exist ("The last gate: re-run the Phase-1 methodology... against the finished, reviewed-and-corrected product") — is absent, so every acceptance criterion is unevidenced (artifacts_present=False; all three CriterionChecks indeterminate).

The executor's only content change was editing audits/design-review.md (a different, upstream node's evidence artifact) — 6 line-citation tweaks (e.g., keymap.rs:365-372 -> 416-425, dashboard.rs:296-361 -> 296-328, app.rs:2213-2221 -> 2235-2247) committed in the current job's two result commits (be28bf2, eff0c06). This is cross-node artifact tampering: a node writing into another node's evidence document, the same class of harm that design-review attempt 1 was explicitly blocked for (documented in the audits/design-review.md header, lines 3-8: "attempt 1 was blocked: it wrote the wrong node's artifact..., and edited the upstream audit's evidence"). A node must only write its own required artifacts.

The node executed while its dependency was unresolved: review-product-coherence is still provisional (deps_status={'review-product-coherence': 'provisional'}) and its required artifact reviews/product-coherence.md does not exist (no reviews/ directory in the worktree). This violates the node's own constraint "Runs only after review-product-coherence corrects the product" and the deliberate ordering recorded in review-product-coherence.yaml ("Runs BEFORE audit-methodology-compliance; this ordering is deliberate", unlocks: audit-methodology-compliance). The audit gate fired before the product review it must follow, so any claim of final compliance would be auditing an unreviewed, uncorrected product.

integrity.reasoning: The work under review does not preserve the node's intended role in any recognizable form. audit-methodology-compliance exists to be the final compliance gate: re-run the methodology and named criteria against the finished, reviewed-and-corrected product and emit audits/methodology-compliance.md with cited evidence. None of that happened: the required artifact is absent from the worktree (artifacts_present=False), the deterministic scan found no audit content, and the job's only file change was a set of line-citation edits to audits/design-review.md — an upstream node's artifact — not the creation of the audit document. Graph integrity is also harmed in two ways. First, the executor wrote into a different node's evidence document (design-review.md), the exact harm the design-review node's attempt 1 was blocked for; this corrupts the separation of evidence ownership the graph depends on — downstream reviewers can no longer trust that each node's artifacts were written by that node. Second, the node ran while its only dependency (review-product-coherence) is provisional with no artifact present, violating the explicit sequencing constraint and the ordering rationale recorded in the neighbor YAML; the final audit was attempted against a product the reviewer never reviewed. Because audit-methodology-compliance is the terminal node with unlocks: [], a false 'done' here would falsely close the entire graph walkthrough, so this must not proceed without human intervention. The correct path: have review-product-coherence complete and be accepted first, then re-run this node to actually produce audits/methodology-compliance.md — and restore audits/design-review.md to the upstream node's authored state (the citation tweaks, though arguably more accurate against the current worktree, were not this node's to make; any corrections belong to design-review or a review of it). Verdict: block. (Lane-1 acceptance adjudication of the three criteria is moot until the artifact exists; this verdict stands on the missing artifact, cross-node editing, and premature execution regardless.)
